target_customer: Developers, ecommerce businesses and AI agent builders that need to automate online purchases; at launch, online shoppers
problem: Retailers rarely offer ordering APIs. Zinc provides one API to search, order, track and return products across many retailers.

founders.name: Max Kolysh
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch 2014-03-14 as one of three MIT friends; not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Doug Feigelson
founders.role: Founder and CEO (now also CEO of Mystro)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as active founder; TechCrunch 2014 names him among MIT friends.

founders.name: John Wang
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former founder; TechCrunch 2014 names him among MIT friends.

competitors.name: Honey
competitors.what: Browser extension that finds promo codes at checkout, compared with the Zinc Save launch product

competitors.name: RetailMeNot
competitors.what: Promo code site shoppers check manually

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating checkout across retailers that have no public ordering API means scraping and browser automation that breaks when sites change.

defensibility.rationale: Scraped integrations must be maintained constantly and could be copied; retailers could block or offer official APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Zinc; Amazon never offered a general purchasing API. Zinc is still operating and says it is profitable.

market_need_then: The launch consumer product sought discounts at checkout on retailers like Amazon and Walmart; the API market need was only an idea in 2014 and grew with ecommerce automation and later AI agents.

branding.domain_note: Used zinc.io and zincapi.com earlier; now uses zinc.com (older pages on zinc.io and zincapi.com still surfaced). Date and price of the zinc.com move not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused and technical; tagline 'secret backbone of e-commerce'.

rebrands.why: Not stated; domain change only, name unchanged.

brand_strength.rationale: Short name but shared by many unrelated Zinc companies (a messaging company and others show up in searches); no brand press or community found.

pivots.from: Zinc Save consumer shopping companion that finds discounts
pivots.to: programmable commerce API (the original idea and current focus)
pivots.why: Not sourced; TechCrunch 2014 says the consumer product was built on an API for buying online, and the company now sells the API.

outcome_analysis: Zinc started in YC Winter 2014 with an ordering API idea and a consumer discount product, stayed essentially bootstrapped, and now sells a purchasing API it says has placed over 21 million orders and runs profitably. It never raised a large round and no exit occurred, so the outcome is a small durable business now helped by AI agent demand.
notes: TechCrunch 2014 describes the company as YC backed and otherwise bootstrapped, based in Palo Alto with three people. Funding figures from aggregators (120K YC seed, 270K total incl. a PPP loan) are unverified and no round recorded; the YC standard deal is not a round. Several CB Insights Zinc profiles belong to other companies. Zinc about page says it is profitable and has processed over 21 million orders, a company claim. Max Kolysh is named by TechCrunch but not the YC page. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
